votes.question_text: What failure mode arises if you register the wrong type of HTTP request customizer (e.g., McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer vs McpAsyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer) for an MCP client transport, and why must the customizer type match the client type?
votes.vote_reasoning: This question requires understanding of why synchronous and asynchronous (reactive) integrations are different — not just which interface to use. Answering correctly shows the student grasps execution models, return-type contracts (blocking vs Publisher/Mono), threading/context propagation, and the concrete failure modes that result when those expectations are violated (ignored customizers, runtime type errors, lost Reactor context, deadlocks). It connects concepts (API compatibility, concurrency model, reactive streams) and tests implications of mismatching components, so it demonstrates deep conceptual understanding rather than rote recall. Score 9: Exceptional learning question.
